rules: Every initial structural candidate is random. Structural mutations and crossover never inspect numerical solver weights or gradients.
The outer search receives only support/query predictive scores from freshly fitted candidate solvers. Gradients optimize coefficients within fixed structures only.
No hidden input blocks, roles, filter count, teacher permutation, or analytic wiring enters proposal generation, mutation, fitness or selection.
Generic choices are the dense ReLU model class, finite complexity budgets, random structural operators and predictive selection; these are not an assertion of zero inductive bias.
Keep separate mask and weight-sharing populations so that early optimizer performance cannot eliminate either family.
Search uses source tasks 0-7; source tasks 8-9 select candidates and numerical/generator settings; tasks 10-11 are audit only.
Freeze bank, generator and hyperparameters before generating independent target tasks. Report unsuccessful structural discovery as such.
Compare AR with whole-bank sampling, one searched structure, independent frequencies, matched fresh random structures, shuffled inputs, mask-only and a tuned dense MLP.
No software tests are created or run. Preserve unrelated work and occupied GPUs.
